habitat: Singly, in small flocks, or occasionally in large numbers at coastal estuaries and lagoons and at inland waters. It feeds on shorelines and in the shallows with a hunched, head-down posture.
summary: A common summer visitor. A tiny, active wader. Non-breeding plumage is sandy-brown above, with feathers edged white, and white below, with a short black bill and black legs. It gives a sharp chit. Newman does not name the months. The Kemp name Little Stint and the code NB were left unchanged.

sources.title: Avibase bird checklist — Kruger National Park

Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

bill.shape: Short. It is slightly longer and more slender than Red-necked Stint.

upperparts.pattern: Non-breeding plumage is sandy-brown above, with the feathers edged white. Dark feather centres make the upperparts more heavily blotched than Red-necked Stint. Worn plumage may look paler.

viewNotes.note: Sandy-brown above with white feather edges, white below, and a short black bill.
Sandy-brown upperparts with white feather edges and darker feather centres.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: A sharp 'chit' or a rapid 'chit-chit-chit…'. No grade A recording from South Africa was found. The selected file is a grade A call from Uzbekistan. The filename is XC185089-Calidris minuta 140508_038,AAB+.MP3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common summer visitor and does not name the months, so status is summer-migrant and monthsPresent is unset. Sandy-brown is not a vocabulary colour, so the upperparts colour is left unset. No grade A recording from South Africa was found; a grade B recording from South Africa exists. The iNaturalist account has no display name, so the login stproc is credited. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^6=64 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 32–128.
